content.text: The ferrata log has the concrete error: `failed to read v1 session 1: no transcript found for checkpoint`. I’m checking the v1 checkpoint tree now to see whether session `1/` is genuinely missing transcript data or whether it’s stored under an unexpected name.

The v1 tree confirms the mismatch: root `metadata.json` advertises a second session transcript at `/37/bdd9250710/1/full.jsonl`, but that file is not present. I’m also checking whether the failed run left a partial v2 copy behind, because that affects what a rerun would do.

This is a malformed v1 checkpoint, not a generic v2 write failure: session `1/` has only `metadata.json`. I’m looking at the v1 metadata-branch commits for that checkpoint to see how the empty second session got recorded.

Ferrata failed because checkpoint `37bdd9250710` is malformed in v1.

The v1 root metadata says the checkpoint has two sessions, and session `1` should have `/37/bdd9250710/1/full.jsonl`, but the actual tree only contains:

```text
0/content_hash.txt
0/context.md
0/full.jsonl
0/metadata.json
0/prompt.txt
1/metadata.json
metadata.json
```

So migration gets through session `0`, then fails reading session `1` with:

```text
failed to read v1 session 1: no transcript found for checkpoint
```

That exact error is in `/Users/ninawork/entire/migrate-v2/ferrata/.entire/logs/entire.log`.

The v1 history shows how it happened: commit `770745d` added only `37/bdd9250710/1/metadata.json` and updated root metadata to advertise a second session. It never added `1/full.jsonl`, `1/content_hash.txt`, or `1/prompt.txt`. That second session also has `checkpoints_count: 0`, so it looks like an empty/stale session record got attached to the checkpoint.

The failed run did leave a partial v2 migration for the valid first session. `refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main` and `/full/current` both have session `0`; there is no session `1` in v2. The migration code fails because it iterates all v1 `summary.Sessions` in [migrate.go](/Users/ninawork/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/migrate.go:200), and `ReadSessionContent` rejects sessions with no transcript in [committed.go](/Users/ninawork/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/committed.go:1040).
I think it should warn when this happens and explain why: that there was not a session for that one.

That makes sense. I’m going to update the v2 migration path so a malformed v1 session entry without transcript is treated as a clear warning and skipped, instead of making the whole checkpoint look like an unexplained hard failure.

I’ve got the relevant pattern: migration currently assumes every session listed by v1 root metadata is readable. I’m going to make the migration loop tolerate `ErrNoTranscript` for an individual v1 session, emit an explicit warning, and still migrate the valid sessions in that checkpoint.

I’m going to edit the migration command and add a regression test that creates a v1 checkpoint with one real session plus one metadata-only phantom session. The expected behavior will be: warning, checkpoint migrates, v2 contains only the real session, no failure count.
